# Results — Study 97 (Balancing-Act) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — hold a fixed
**60% SPY / 40% IEF** blend, **rebalanced on the first trading day of each year** (drift in
between), charge **2 bps** one-way on rebalance turnover — run on the **total-return** tapes
and pinned against **100% stocks (SPY)** and a **60/40 (SPY/TLT)** variant. Sharpes are
**excess-of-cash** (SHY, 1-3y Treasuries, the cash proxy) so the part-bond blend and 100%
stocks race like-for-like. As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprints to confirm you hold
the same tapes.*

## The race — annual rebalance, 2 bps/rebalance, excess-of-cash Sharpe

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (xs) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **60/40 (SPY/IEF)** | 8.63% | **10.2%** | **0.655** | **−29.8%** |
| 60/40 (SPY/TLT) | 8.96% | 10.5% | 0.683 | −27.6% |
| 100% stocks (SPY) | **11.20%** | 18.8% | 0.541 | −55.2% |

## Is the risk-adjusted improvement real and robust?

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| 60/40 (SPY/IEF) − SPY Sharpe (excess-of-cash) | **+0.115** |
| HAC *t* on the daily (60/40 − SPY) excess-return difference | **−2.28** (\|t\| > 2) |
| Block-bootstrap Sharpe-difference point | **+0.115** |
| 95% bootstrap CI (circular block, 21d, 2000 reps) | **[+0.022, +0.207]** — excludes 0 |
| 60/40 wins the Sharpe race in … of resamples | **99%** |

The Sharpe improvement **clears the bar**: the autocorrelation-robust *t* on the daily
return difference is **−2.28** (the blend earns *less per day* but with far less variance, so
the negative-sign mean difference is significant), and the bootstrap CI for the Sharpe
*difference* sits entirely above zero. → Signal **REAL** on the 2002-2021-dominated tape.

## The cushion claim — "bonds cushion every equity crash"?

Rolling 63-day SPY/IEF correlation: **mean −0.26**, range **[−0.83, +0.67]**, positive on
**23% of days**. Bonds were a diversifier *on average* — but the correlation is **regime-
dependent**, not a constant negative law.

Every SPY drawdown deeper than −10%, with the bond legs' total return over the *same* window:

| Equity drawdown | SPY | IEF | TLT |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2002-08 → 2002-10 | −18.9% | **+5.4%** | +6.8% |
| 2007-10 → 2009-03 (GFC) | −55.2% | **+20.2%** | +25.1% |
| 2015-07 → 2016-02 | −13.0% | **+7.4%** | +14.8% |
| 2018-01 → 2018-02 | −10.1% | **−1.2%** | −3.8% |
| 2018-09 → 2018-12 | −19.3% | **+3.4%** | +4.5% |
| 2020-02 → 2020-03 (COVID) | −33.7% | **+6.4%** | +14.2% |
| **2022-01 → 2022-10** | **−24.5%** | **−15.4%** | **−29.3%** |
| 2025-02 → 2025-04 | −18.8% | **+2.7%** | +0.8% |

Bonds (IEF) rose in **6 of 8** equity crashes. **2022 is the decisive failure**: as stocks
fell ~24%, IEF fell **−15.4%** and TLT **−31.3%** — the cushion became an *anchor*. For the
full 2022 calendar year: **SPY −18.2%, IEF −15.2%, TLT −31.2%, 60/40 (SPY/IEF) −17.0%** —
the blend barely helped. → 3rd axis **"Bonds always cushion?" → NOT SUPPORTED**.

## How to read it

- **The risk-adjusted improvement is real on this tape.** 60/40 cut volatility nearly in
  half (10.2% vs 18.8%) and roughly halved the worst drawdown (−29.8% vs −55.2%), lifting
  the excess-of-cash Sharpe from 0.541 to 0.655 — and that gain survives HAC inference and a
  block bootstrap. → Signal **REAL**.
- **But it is investable *with caveats*, not a free lunch.** It is two cheap, infinitely
  liquid ETFs on an annual rebalance — a sensible default core. The catch is that 60/40
  **gave up 2.6 pts/yr of CAGR** (8.63% vs 11.20%) for the calmer ride, and much of the
  Sharpe edge is the **historic bond bull market** (a yield decline you were *paid* for —
  beta, not a structural law). → Tradability **INVESTABLE (with caveats)**.
- **The cushion is not universal.** It worked in 6 of 8 crashes but *failed in 2022*, when a
  rate shock drove stocks and bonds down together. "Bonds cushion *every* crash" is **NOT
  SUPPORTED**.
